comment: The Jayway dialect of a facet path (anyof, noneof, == null, != null) is no longer read (0.17, issue #128): the kernel refuses it with one sentence that names the standard form (RFC 9535). Read by the kernel's own tests (lib.rs), ViewpointKernelTest and conformance.test.js; the command line says it as `error: facet <name>: <error>`. `accepted` are paths that look alike and are standard.

refused.error: the facet path `$.application..relationships[?(@.qualifiers anyof ['REST', 'x'])]` uses `@.qualifiers anyof ['REST', 'x']`, which is not JSONPath (RFC 9535) and is no longer read: write `@.qualifiers[?(@ == 'REST' || @ == 'x')]`

the facet path `$..relationships[?(@.qualifiers noneof ['REST'])]` uses `@.qualifiers noneof ['REST']`, which is not JSONPath (RFC 9535) and is no longer read: write `(@.qualifiers && !@.qualifiers[?(@ == 'REST')])`
the facet path `$..relationships[?(@.qualifiers == null)]` uses `@.qualifiers == null`, which is not JSONPath (RFC 9535) and is no longer read: write `!@.qualifiers`
the facet path `$..relationships[?(@.label != null)]` uses `@.label != null`, which is not JSONPath (RFC 9535) and is no longer read: write `@.label`

the facet path `$..relationships[?(@.label == 'x' && @.qualifiers == null && @.tags != null)]` uses `@.qualifiers == null`, which is not JSONPath (RFC 9535) and is no longer read: write `!@.qualifiers`

the facet path `$..relationships[?(@.qualifiers anyof ['a]b', "c,d"] && @.label == 'x')]` uses `@.qualifiers anyof ['a]b', "c,d"]`, which is not JSONPath (RFC 9535) and is no longer read: write `@.qualifiers[?(@ == 'a]b' || @ == "c,d")]`
